pure-announcement.rationale: An ICLR 2026 research paper introducing a trained coordination mechanism, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept covers learned multi-agent orchestration; weak-to-strong generalization is about supervision quality, not RL-discovered coordination topologies.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Claims are anchored to a primary arXiv/ICLR paper with named benchmarks (LiveCodeBench, GPQA) a reader can verify.

durability.rationale: The transferable mechanism — coordination topology and per-agent prompting can be learned end-to-end via RL rather than hand-designed, generalizing via randomized agent pools — outlives the specific benchmark numbers cited.

actionability.rationale: The pattern requires RL-training a dedicated conductor model, so for most builders it reframes what is possible in orchestration rather than giving a step they can take today.

atomicity.rationale: One idea — a learned conductor that discovers coordination strategies over worker LLMs — with recursion and pool-randomization as elaborations of it, statable in a paragraph.
